newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde Oct 1.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- Israel fears an upsurge of violence if Washington emergency summit on Middle East crisis fails.

-- Carmakers to adopt price cuts policy to fend off expected drop in car sales linked to the expiry of a government incentive package for buyers of new cars, which boosted September car registrations 85.7 percent.
-- Radio pager service Tamtam to open operating center in Poitiers, expected to create 480 jobs.
-- Cie Generale des Eaux deputy managing director Jean-Marc Espalioux may become Accor chairman.
-- Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) expected to post at least 500-million-franc profit for the first half, ahead of privatisation.
-- Analysts still expect Eurotunnel and bankers to reach debt-restructuring agreement soon.

-- Government plans budget austerity to year 2001, expects to cut budget deficit by 20 to 26 billion francs a year over that period, bring it down in 2001 to two percent of GDP in national accounting terms.
